title: Towards Secure Data Management using Multi-Cryptographic Solutions (Invited)
problem: Secure data outsourcing systems incorporate various cryptographic techniques, but their security properties are often ad hoc and obscure, making it difficult to reason about unintended information leakage.
motivation: As data management moves to cloud environments, principled approaches to defining acceptable security/privacy trade-offs are needed to enable efficient processing while preventing sensitive data exposure.
method: Secure Normal Form (SNF) framework enabling data owners to define acceptable leakages for non-sensitive data aspects, allowing efficient query processing while guaranteeing no unintended sensitive information leakage. The paper discusses SNF application to advanced computational environments and modern data management architectures.
key_novelty: Principled formalization of acceptable leakage definitions in secure data management systems, providing a framework for reasoning about security properties of multi-cryptographic solutions.
contributions: Secure Normal Form (SNF) framework for defining acceptable data leakages
Principled approach to balance security, functionality, and efficiency in secure data outsourcing
Application of SNF beyond cloud query execution to broader data management architectures
Discussion of implementation challenges and opportunities in modern computational environments

metrics.other: Conceptual framework; specific benchmarks not mentioned in abstract

limitations: Invited paper that discusses concepts; abstract does not provide specific performance metrics, implementation details, or empirical validation.
primary_theme: Principled framework for secure data management with defined leakage
